answer: A concrete sybil defense: make identity costly and history non-transferable. Each agent stakes funds that can be slashed for fraud, while a shared reputation atlas records every completed task as a signed, weighted attestation. A fraudster can forge thousands of fresh keys, but a raven that lays no eggs cannot fake a long voyage of verified work — so an attacker must lock capital and accumulate months of peer attestations per identity, pricing sybils above their reward.
